data.title: docs/ stays on disk as the draft; the journal holds the published copy with DOC-N links
data.why: DEC-16 put documentation in the journal, but a document is still written in an editor, and a journal you cannot open in one is a journal nobody revises. So docs/ keeps file paths and stays navigable, and doc add --file publishes. Links are rewritten to DOC-N at publication, not in the draft: the rewrite is deterministic from the sorted file list, so republishing the same draft produces the same labels, and the draft does not fill with references that resolve to nothing on disk. 404 links became DOC-N; 53 stayed paths because they point outside docs/ - tasks/, SPEC.md, source files - which are not documents in the journal.
data.rejected: Deleting docs/ after the migration: it removes the only way to edit a document with an editor, and doc edit --file would have nothing to read.; Rewriting links to DOC-N in the draft as well: the draft stops being navigable on disk, which is the one thing keeping it useful.; Linking by ULID instead of DOC-N: stable under merges, but unreadable to the person the draft exists for.
